items.title: Bridges are now live in the Freehold mobile app, starting with RIO and Base
items.text: Freehold says bridges are live, beginning with RIO and Base bridges. More tokens and networks will roll out in phases, and each one will be announced when it goes live. Derek told the Freehold group to update the app and try it.

items.title: Freehold tells its waitlist to watch their inbox for updates coming soon
items.text: Freehold posted a reminder that people on its list should keep an eye on their inbox for updates coming soon. No details or date were given.

items.title: Derek explains why large companies resist third-party tokenized stocks
items.text: Asked about companies objecting to their stock being tokenized on an exchange, Derek says they see no benefit in a tokenized version they cannot control or see into, only added risk. He adds that Robinhood's stock tokens are not available to US persons.

items.title: Freehold: investor whitelist and transfer rules for tokens kept on-chain
items.text: Freehold says issuers can whitelist investors and set transfer rules, with the record of who holds a token and how much kept on-chain instead of in a spreadsheet. Getting started is free.

items.title: Freehold team to look into KYC issues reported by Balkans-region users
items.text: Derek says non-US exchanges follow different OFAC standards than the ones Freehold has to meet, and that the Balkans region can be problematic with various compliance groups. The team will inquire about the KYC failures raised in the Freehold group.

items.title: Derek: team is building a better block explorer
items.text: Asked how to get staking history for tax purposes, Derek says the team is working on a better block explorer and that it is needed. He says it was not a priority for the small team, which is taking on the extra work internally.

items.title: Derek: claims portal coming soon, UI almost done
items.text: Asked about claims, Derek says the portal should be ready soon and the team is focused on it. It needed some mainnet updates and the UI is almost done. KYC'd v1 accounts will be easier to match to a Freehold account; other accounts need a manual review that may take longer.

items.title: Team completes phase 2 of the recovery plan, staking claims are next
items.text: Eduardo says the team has completed phase 2 of the recovery plan and is now focused on the part that lets users claim their staking positions. He says this will eventually be available on the dashboard.

items.title: No redelegation from offline compromised validators until recovery is complete
items.text: Eduardo says wallets compromised in the incident cannot redelegate away from an offline validator until the recovery process is complete. Derek says rewards keep accruing while the network and the validator are online. The team asked validators to shut down without causing slashing.

items.title: Derek says holders are closer to getting access to their tokens
items.text: Asked in the Official Telegram group whether holders are closer to getting access to their tokens, Derek answered yes. No timeline was given.

items.title: Derek: a validator shutting down could risk slashing; team asks it to stay up longer
items.text: Derek Boirun says he may have misunderstood earlier and that there could be a risk of slashing. He asked a team member to request that the validator keep running a little longer, so people have time to claim their wallets and unstake.

items.title: Derek: team building a better block explorer for locked v1 staking accounts
items.text: Derek says the team is building a better block explorer so holders can see the v1 accounts that were staking and got locked. He is not sure it will be ready before the claims portal.

items.title: Derek: Freehold claims portal is unrelated to the RIO price
items.text: Derek Boirun told the Official Telegram group the Freehold claims portal has nothing to do with the price of RIO and asked members to stop spreading speculation linking the two. He said such posts will be deleted.

items.title: Freehold: issuers set transfer rules up front when tokenizing an asset
items.text: Freehold says that when an asset is tokenized on the platform, the issuer sets the transfer rules at the start: who can hold it, who can trade it and under what conditions. It describes getting started as free.

items.title: Freehold car tokens: primary purchases in USDC, BTC or ETH, RIO pairs for secondary
items.text: Derek says primary purchases of the team-sponsored car tokens will be made in USDC, BTC or ETH, with RIO trading pairs for secondary trading. Primary pools on the native DEX will pair with RIO. Bridging ETH and BTC is only needed for the DEX, not for token purchases.

items.title: Derek: a validator shutting down does not slash or lose delegators' staked coins
items.text: Asked about a validator that has announced it will shut down, Derek said delegators are not slashed and staked coins are not lost after a shutdown. He confirmed staked coins will be retrievable and said updates will come when available.

items.title: Derek: claims are the current priority; Algorand and Stellar holders need take no action
items.text: Asked whether the Freehold app or the claims process comes first, Derek said claims are the current priority. Asked whether Algorand and Stellar holders should move tokens into the Freehold wallet, he said no action is necessary.

items.title: Freehold explains how the Freehold Collection works and opens early access requests
items.text: Freehold outlined the Freehold Collection model: the team sources each car, every vehicle is structured as its own fractionalized ownership opportunity, and holders own a share accessible through Freehold. Early access can be requested.

items.title: Freehold on/off ramp: MoonPay for now, proper ramp comes later
items.text: Derek says MoonPay works for both buying and selling on Freehold but does not handle high volume. A proper on/off ramp will be added after other items are completed and launched. Until then, holders can get stablecoins from Coinbase and withdraw them to Freehold.

items.title: Freehold has chosen the first car for the Freehold Collection
items.text: The Freehold team says the first car in the Freehold Collection is documented and almost ready. It is not naming the car yet. The early access list will hear first.

items.title: Derek: Freehold is now the product and the team's focus
items.text: Derek says Freehold is the app and where the team's current efforts are focused, and that the earlier Realio product is gone. He asked members of the Realio Network chat to join the Freehold group.

items.title: Freehold KYC: support tickets and the verifier decide cases, not the founder
items.text: Derek says founders do not approve KYC for users. Holders with an open support ticket will be asked for information, or the third-party KYC provider cannot approve them for a valid reason. He advises following up on the ticket.

items.title: Derek: claims updates will be posted on Freehold, where the claims portal will be
items.text: Asked about tokens lost on other wallets, Derek said the updates will be on Freehold, where the claims portal will be. No further claims details were given.

items.title: Derek: transaction history for tax can be pulled with a wallet address
items.text: Asked for account transfer data for accounting and tax purposes, Derek said a wallet address and any block explorer or accounting software is all that is needed.

items.title: Derek: there is no Freehold credit card
items.text: Asked whether Freehold has a credit card, Derek said no.

items.title: Freehold Collection opens early access requests for shares in collector cars
items.text: Freehold says the Freehold Collection is a new way to own a share of extraordinary collector cars and is taking early access requests. Derek says the SP3 has reached collector car unicorn status, with U.S. spec cars going for $15m.

items.title: Derek: Freehold stablecoin bridge and native DEX are coming
items.text: Asked about a stablecoin bridge and a native DEX for Freehold, Derek said both are coming as well, after saying that the tokenization wave is coming.

items.title: Derek: no claims update, process will be slow and drawn out
items.text: Derek says there is no update on claims and that the process will be slow and drawn out, with no single event where everyone gets tokens. He added that Realio v1 was hacked and no longer exists, and asked holders for patience.

items.title: Team says tokenization fee details in the old whitepaper are outdated
items.text: Asked whether the fee split in the documentation still applies, Derek said it is old language from an outdated whitepaper and that things will evolve with the market and applicable regulations.

items.title: Freehold KYC: team to check with its verifier on locations missing from the list
items.text: Derek says the team will check with the verification provider about a location missing from the Freehold KYC list, adding that China has its own difficulties.

items.title: Derek: team cannot transact with people in sanctioned countries
items.text: Derek says the team legally cannot transact with people in OFAC-sanctioned countries. A decentralized way to claim anonymously will only be looked at once the current work is done and there is more bandwidth, if it is possible at all.

items.title: No further updates on the security incident
items.text: Derek reposted the reminder that the latest information on the security incident is on the incident page and said there are no further updates at this time. Updates will be provided when they become available.

items.title: Realio warns of impersonators and says official claims process is not live yet
items.text: Realio says @realio_network is its only official X account and that it will never ask for seed phrases, funds to verify assets, or wallet connections to unofficial claims sites. The official claims process will be announced through verified channels when available.

items.title: Districts login issues fixed after security upgrades
items.text: Districts says the temporary login issues that followed recent security and authentication upgrades are fixed. Logging in works again, with stronger security in place.

items.title: Freehold promotes Tokenization Studio as a single non-custodial workflow
items.text: Freehold says its Tokenization Studio takes an asset to a live token in one non-custodial workflow, with no build team needed. The studio is free to start.

items.title: Derek: frozen staking addresses, legal claim process still being worked on
items.text: Derek says staking addresses used through the original Realio web app were frozen by a validator network update. Work to let users legally claim ownership of those addresses is ongoing, and he says it is all solely to protect user assets.

items.title: Derek explains how supply caps can change on each chain
items.text: Derek says the supply cap on the native network is coded in and would need all validators to agree to change. On Ethereum and BSC, a change would need a new token contract. He did not give a combined cap figure.

items.title: Derek: the wallet flagged as a team wallet is not one
items.text: Derek says a wallet circulating as a team wallet is not one. He asks holders to stop labelling whale wallets as team wallets, because it makes those wallets targets for address spoofing scams.
